brief: Mobile and desktop app where users view CGM glucose readings and log meals. Frequent meals can be saved for quick re-logging. The client wants a first demo within two months.

questions.text: Which glucose monitoring devices does the app need to work with?
Are there legal, security, or compliance requirements?
Is the deadline fixed, and what happens if it slips?
What does success look like in 3 to 6 months?
Who will use this product, and roughly how many people?
Why is this a priority right now?

chunks:
[1] Priyanka (internal): Good morning everyone. Let's dive right into our discovery session for the CGM and meal tracking app.
[2] Ouali (client): Good morning Priyanka, Alex. Glad to connect.
[3] Sarah (client): Morning all.
[4] Priyanka (internal): Let's start with the sensors. Which glucose monitoring hardware must we integrate with initially?
[5] Ouali (client): Well, um, our clinical trial patients primarily use Abbott FreeStyle Libre 3. We definitely need Abbott LibreLinkUp API integration first. Later on we might look at Dexcom G7, but Phase 1 is strictly Abbott Libre 3.
[6] Alex (internal): Got it, Abbott Libre 3 is our primary device target for the initial release.
[7] Priyanka (internal): And what about compliance and privacy rules?
[8] Sarah (client): That is non-negotiable. Because we handle continuous blood glucose records, the platform must be fully HIPAA compliant from day one, with all patient health data encrypted at rest using AES-256.
[9] Alex (internal): Completely agreed. We will enforce end-to-end encryption and HIPAA audit logging across all microservices.
[10] Ouali (client): As for the deadline, our board demonstration is scheduled for December 18. This demo deadline is completely non-negotiable because our Series A funding milestone hinges on it.

[11] Priyanka (internal): Regarding the pilot rollout, roughly how many people will be testing this first version?
[12] Ouali (client): We are estimating maybe around 500 beta diabetic patients across three endocrinology clinics, though depending on clinic onboarding it might be anywhere from 300 to 700.
[13] Alex (internal): Okay, roughly 300 to 700 trial participants.
[14] Sarah (client): We also made a firm decision yesterday regarding platforms: we are launching exclusively on iOS first. Android support is explicitly postponed to Phase 2.
[15] Alex (internal): Makes sense to focus on iOS for the pilot.
[16] Priyanka (internal): And for meal logging, does MVP include food barcode scanning?
[17] Ouali (client): No, barcode scanning is out of scope for the demo. Just manual meal descriptions, photos, and quick-save favorites.
[18] Ouali (client): I will send over the Abbott LibreLinkUp API sandbox credentials and developer documentation by tomorrow afternoon.
[19] Sarah (client): And I will email the HIPAA compliance requirements checklist and patient consent form templates by Thursday.
[20] Alex (internal): Perfect. I will review the Abbott specs and share our initial system architecture draft by this Friday.
[21] Priyanka (internal): Excellent. We will reconvene next Monday.
